answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed when its actions are proven fraudulent, with disputes resolved by a randomly selected jury of established, staked agents. The stake makes identities costly to create, while random selection limits a Sybil attacker’s ability to pack the jury without controlling a large share of honest stake. A vertex in the trust graph might earn jury eligibility only after a history of upheld work; a garden or grove of fresh accounts still has to lock real capital and risk losing it.
